articles.headline: White Sox blow 6-run lead and fall out of 1st place in AL Central with 11-8 loss to Tigers
articles.description: — Hao-Yu Lee and Riley Greene each hit a two-run homer in a five-run eighth inning as the Detroit Tigers rallied from six down to beat the Chicago White Sox 11-8 on Friday night.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- — Hao-Yu Lee and Riley Greene each hit a two-run homer in a five-run eighth inning as the Detroit Tigers rallied from six down to beat the Chicago White Sox 11-8 on Friday night.


              Chicago (78-76) trails first-place Cleveland by one game in the AL Central with eight remaining, although the White Sox own the head-to-head tiebreaker after winning the season series. Chicago has a one-game lead for the final American League wild card.


              Detroit (73-81) trailed 8-2 after Miguel Vargas hit his 32nd homer for the White Sox — a two-run shot in the third inning.


              Chicago right fielder Tristan Peters left the game in the fifth after crashing into the wall in right-center on Kevin McGonigle's bases-loaded triple that cut it to 8-5 and chased rookie starter David Sandlin. 


              Lee had a two-out RBI double off Chris Murphy in the sixth to make it 8-6. 


              Lee tied it against Sean Newcomb (2-5) with his 10th homer and Greene followed with his 21st — off Bryan Hudson — later in the inning. Dillon Dingler had a go-ahead single in between the homers. Lee finished with four of the Tigers' 16 hits. 


              Colson Montgomery hit a three-run double with two outs in the first as Chicago scored six unearned runs off Andrew Sears in his third career start to take a 6-1 lead. 


              Colt Keith doubled and scored from second on a wild pitch to put Detroit up 1-0 in the first. McGonigle's RBI single cut it to 6-2 in the third.


              Drew Sommers (2-4) struck out five in two perfect innings for the win, and Kenley Jansen pitched the ninth for his 21st save in 27 opportunities this season. It was the 497th save of his career.


              Sandlin pitched four innings in his fifth career start and allowed five runs on seven hits. 


              Up next
              Tigers RHP Jackson Jobe (2-2, 3.89 ERA) starts Saturday opposite White Sox RHP Sean Burke (9-7, 3.47). The game time was moved up to 1:10 p.m. because of the weather.


              ------

articles.headline: Corey Seager's RBI double helps Rangers beat sloppy Blue Jays 7-1 and close gap in playoff race
articles.description: — Corey Seager had an RBI double in a four-run second inning fueled by a throwing error, and the Texas Rangers beat the Toronto Blue Jays 7-1 on Friday night in the opener of a series matching AL playoff chasers.
articles.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- — Corey Seager had an RBI double in a four-run second inning fueled by a throwing error, and the Texas Rangers beat the Toronto Blue Jays 7-1 on Friday night in the opener of a series matching AL playoff chasers.


              The Rangers (77-77) reached .500 for a majors-leading 23rd time and pulled within one game of the White Sox for the third and final AL wild-card spot, although Chicago has the tiebreaker. The defending AL champion Blue Jays (76-78) are two games back in the wild-card race.


              Texas also closed the gap on Houston by pulling even with the Astros atop the AL West, but the Rangers would have to win the division outright to finish ahead of their in-state rival. Houston lost to Atlanta 6-2.


              The Rangers took the lead in the second on Evan Carter's bases-loaded grounder that scored Wyatt Langford, and Jake Burger also came home when shortstop Ernie Clement's throw trying to force him out at third bounced wide of the bag into foul territory. Seager made it 4-0 with his double.


              Dylan Cease (11-6) walked a season-high six among his first 15 batters and was replaced with two outs in the third after throwing 38 balls and 36 strikes.


              Five of the Texas runs were unearned as the Blue Jays walked 10 and had three throwing errors, two by third baseman Kazuma Okamoto.


              Trevor Williams (2-0) finished with four scoreless innings after starter Kumar Rocker took a 4-0 lead into the fifth but couldn't finish and was replaced by Tyler Alexander.


              Toronto's Nathan Lukes had the longest active hitting streak in the majors stopped at 13 games when he was replaced by pinch-hitter Davis Schneider in the fifth. Lukes was 0 for 2 with a deep liner that Carter, the center fielder, ran down at the wall in right center.


              Up next
              Blue Jays RHP José Soriano (12-7, 3.56 ERA) is set to face Texas RHP Cal Quantrill (9-5, 2.90) on Saturday.


              ------


              This story is updated to correct that the Rangers scored five unearned runs, not six.

articles.headline: CJ Abrams joins 30-30 club as Nationals rout Cardinals 9-1
articles.description: — CJ Abrams became the 52nd player to join the 30-30 club, Cade Cavalli threw his 200th strikeout of the year, and the Washington Nationals took down the St. Louis Cardinals 9-1 on Friday night.
articles.body:
ST. LOUIS -- — CJ Abrams became the 52nd player to join the 30-30 club, Cade Cavalli threw his 200th strikeout of the year, and the Washington Nationals took down the St. Louis Cardinals 9-1 on Friday night.


              Abrams joined the Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong as the only players to hit 30 homers and steal 30 bases this season. He is just the second National to do it, joining Alfonso Soriano in 2006.


              Cavalli (13-5) struck out the side in the first, and finished with six strikeouts and four hits in five innings of work.


              His 200th strikeout came on his final pitch of the night, and he became the fifth Nationals pitcher with a 200-strikeout season — joining Patrick Corbin, Gio Gonzalez, Max Scherzer, and Stephen Strasburg — just hours after inking a four-year, $47 million contract extension. 


              The Nats scored three runs in the first, started by Abrams' RBI single. Abrams then stole his 30th base, and an errant throw from Cardinals catcher Leo Bernal let Dylan Crews come around to score. Brady House added an RBI groundout before the end of the frame.


              Crews started a four-run third with his 12th homer of the season, a two-run shot to right, and Yohandy Morales added a two-run double.


              Daylen Lile hit a sacrifice fly in the fourth and James Wood had an RBI double in the sixth to round out the scoring.


              Bernal had two hits for the Cardinals. Kyle Leahy (10-5) allowed a season-high seven runs (six earned) on five hits. He walked three and struck out one.


              With the loss, St. Louis was mathematically eliminated from playoff contention.


              Up next
              Nats LHP Andrew Alvarez (2-6, 3.35 ERA) faces Cardinals RHP Michael McGreevy (7-9, 3.83) as the series continues on Saturday.


              ------

articles.body:
Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists. 

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 2 Buzz 

Week 2 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 2

Biggest concerns heading into Week 2

Players with early starts

Zay Flowers, WR, Ravens (hamstring): Flowers was on his way to a monstrous Week 1 performance when he exited because of a hamstring injury that caused him to miss the first two days of practice this week. He did return to the field Friday, giving him a chance to suit up in Week 2. However, he is officially doubtful to go. If Flowers were to suit up this week, there is added risk that he could once again exit early.

If he sits, Rashod Bateman would be the No. 1 WR option for Lamar Jackson and would bring upside for fantasy, even if the floor is low. Mark Andrews should be started as a TE1. Some streaming options this week include Jalen Coker, Caleb Douglas, Devaughn Vele, plus a sleeper for this week, DeMario Douglas.

Joe Burrow, QB, Bengals (back): Burrow is dealing with back soreness and is listed as questionable but is expected to start. The quarterback stated that it would be "ridiculous" if the injury caused him to miss Week 2. Even in a tough matchup like the Texans, Burrow is a fantasy QB1.

If you want to avoid the matchup, Jaxson Dart and Brock Purdy are realistic options that a fantasy manager could have backing up Burrow. If you're skittish, those two could be started over him. However, for most of you, the choice should be to ride with Burrow.

TreVeyon Henderson, RB, Patriots (ankle): After missing the Patriots' opener because of an ankle injury, Henderson returned to practice this week and says he is "ready to go" for Week 2. Henderson will share work in the backfield with Rhamondre Stevenson. However, he is the more explosive option and therefore brings more fantasy upside.

Henderson can be played over Quinshon Judkins, MarShawn Lloyd, Tony Pollard, J.K. Dobbins, Rico Dowdle, Blake Corum, Kenny Gainwell and Jonathon Brooks.

Jalen Coker, WR, Panthers (ankle): After a huge Week 1 performance, Coker was limited in practice to start the week because of an ankle injury. He was able to log a full practice Friday and was removed from the injury report, meaning he will play in Week 2. While the Panthers will not often have "scorefests" like they did in Week 1, Coker's usage jumps off the screen. He saw nine targets -- three of the deep variety -- and finished with 138 yards and a touchdown, while narrowly missing a second score.

articles.headline: Source: Former Mexico boss Aguirre close to taking over struggling Valencia
articles.description: Former Mexico boss Javier Aguirre has emerged as the leading candidate to fill Valencia's coaching vacancy, a source told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：前メキシコ代表監督のアギーレ氏、低迷するバレンシアの監督就任に接近
articles.descriptionJa: 前メキシコ代表監督のハビエル・アギーレ氏が、バレンシアの監督空席を埋める最有力候補として浮上していると関係者がESPNに語りました。
articles.body:
Valencia has stepped up talks with Javier Aguirre for their vacant coaching job, and a formal offer is expected to be made to the former Mexico boss in the coming days, a source told ESPN's Rodra.

The LaLiga side sacked Carlos Corberán last Sunday and immediately appointed Braulio Vázquez as sporting director to lead the search for a new coach.

Vázquez has been weighing several options, but a source confirms that Aguirre is currently the frontrunner. Ernesto Valverde was also on Valencia's shortlist, but he declined to manage this season after concluding his tenure with Athletic Club.

Valencia sit in the relegation zone after picking up just four points from their first six games.

Aguirre, 67, guided Mexico to the Round of 16 at the last World Cup before they were eliminated by England at the Azteca Stadium. After he finished his deal with Mexico -- a national team he managed across three separate spells, including the 2002 World Cup -- his assistant and 'El Tri' legend, Rafael Márquez, took over as head coach.

He has already fielded approaches from other teams, but the prospect of returning to LaLiga is his preferred option, a source added.

'El Vasco' boasts an extensive career in the Spanish league, with managerial stints at Atlético Madrid, Osasuna, Espanyol, Zaragoza, Leganés, and Mallorca.

Aguirre's potential appointment would be warmly welcomed by the Valencia squad, who view him as a manager with proven experience in lifting teams out of relegation battles, sources closed to the team said.

articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, and teams across the league have been busy making moves. Free agency officially began June 30.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions this offseason, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

Sept. 18: Heat give Larsson a new deal

Pelle Larsson terms: Four years, $60 million, with a mutual option in the fourth year

Grade: B

At summer league in Las Vegas this year, I had a conversation with various NBA folks about the Miami Heat. We were talking about the Heat's lineup possibilities around Giannis Antetokounmpo and how they might build a winner with depleted depth. One clear conclusion from this conversation was that Pelle Larsson was going to get a lot of minutes because Heat coach Erik Spoelstra adores him.

The 25-year-old Swedish guard was a steal at the No. 44 pick in the 2024 draft, and he took a big step forward last season, averaging 11.4 points, 3.5 rebounds and 3.4 assists. The Heat also trust him as a lead defender on the perimeter. He ranked fourth on the team in starts and fifth in total minutes last season.

Larsson profiles as a high-floor, low-ceiling player, given his age and skill set. Most prominently, a shaky 3-point shot (33% in his career) means he's not truly a 3-and-D player but rather a jack of all trades who fits the Heat's preferred ethos with his hustle and stamina.

Still, that high floor means a $15 million average for Larsson is a reasonable value for Miami, and this new deal will carry him through most of his prime years. Larsson must be happy with his new deal, given that his rookie contract was worth only $5.4 million over three years. Spoelstra must be happy to lock up one of his favorite players for the long term, too.

Sept. 18: George, Jazz agree to extension

Keyonte George terms: Five years, $157.5 million

Grade: C+

George was one of the breakout players of the 2025-26 season, averaging 23.6 points and 6.1 assists while making 37% of his 3-pointers. He also boosted his efficiency from 7-8% below average in his first two seasons to 5% above average last year, which made him one of the top offensive guards in the sport.

On its own, that trajectory -- combined with George's age, as he'll turn 23 in November -- makes him more than worthy of this new rookie extension, which will pay him an average of $31.5 million per year. articles.body:
NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 18

Pistons, Thompson reach five-year, $155 million extension

Detroit Pistons All-Defensive forward Ausar Thompson has agreed to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN.

Thompson lands the fully guaranteed extension after making first-team All-Defense and finishing third in Defensive Player of the Year voting last season. The 23-year-old averaged 9.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 0.9 blocks in 2025-26 while leading the NBA in steals per game (2.0).

Heat, Larsson agree to four-year, $60 million extension

Miami Heat guard Pelle Larsson has agreed to a new four-year, $60 million contract extension, with a mutual option for the 2030-31 season, Austin Brown and Steven Heumann of CAA Sports told ESPN on Friday.

A second-round find in the 2024 draft, the 6-foot-5 guard avoids restricted free agency next summer and locks in a new deal with a mutual option that fully guarantees $60 million while allowing either side to opt in on 2030.

Jazz, George agree on a five-year, rookie-scale extension

Utah Jazz guard Keyonte George have agreed on a five-year, $157.5 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania and Tim MacMahon. George was the No. 16 pick in the 2023 draft and has averaged 17.2 points and 5.3 assists per game in his three seasons with the Jazz.

Sept. 17

Bey, Pelicans agree to three-year extension

New Orleans Pelicans' Saddiq Bey agreed to a three-year, $55.5 million contract extension with the franchise, plus a trade kicker, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Bey averaged a career-high 17.7 points per game last season after missing all of the 2024-25 season with a torn ACL.

Sept. 16

Kings remain interested in Duren

The Sacramento Kings continue to loom in the background of Jalen Duren's restricted free agency with the incumbent Detroit Pistons.

Kings general manager Scott Perry met with Duren for dinner in Miami in early July and has maintained a level of steady interest in the ultimate outcome of Duren's free agency, though a path to acquire Duren this summer remains blocked.
